extraction_scope: worker-6 source-reviewed mechanism adjudication from XML/PDF/supplement locators

mechanism_claims.claim_text: CPP-KR12 increases bacterial membrane permeability relative to KR12 in Gram-negative bacteria, supported by SYTOX Green uptake and E. coli SEM morphology; S. aureus membrane permeability is lower and is not overcalled as the same mechanism.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: CPP-KR12 and KR12 in E. coli / P. aeruginosa / S. aureus comparisons
mechanism_claims.limitations: Directly supports membrane permeability/disruption context, not a single molecular target.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: CPP-KR12 shows stronger DNA binding than KR12/CPP in gel retardation context, but this is mechanistic context rather than proof that DNA binding is the sole antibacterial target.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Do not promote DNA binding to primary mode of action without additional causal assays.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: KR12 and CPP-KR12 reduce LPS-stimulated inflammatory cytokine expression in RAW264.7 cells, with CPP alone handled in the supplement as a separate negative/comparator context.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: KR12, CPP, CPP-KR12 in RAW264.7 cells
mechanism_claims.limitations: Host-cell anti-inflammatory expression response, not direct antimicrobial killing mechanism.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Silica entrapment improves CPP-KR12 delivery/stability context, including retained residual antibacterial activity after trypsin and localized particle delivery; this is a formulation/stability mechanism rather than a new peptide target.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Exact figure-derived values are recorded only where supported by prose; image-only quantification is not fabricated.

supplementary_checked.finding: Supplement PDF contains Table S1 nomenclature, Table S2 MIC comparison p-values, and supplemental figures; no additional exact peptide sequence or database assay row replaces the primary XML/PDF evidence.
